title_tag: 7 Best Dinner Cruises in Dubai (2026): Prices Compared
meta_description: Dhow, mega-yacht or canal? 7 Dubai dinner cruises compared on route, buffet vs set menu, open bar, shows and price per hour, from €22 to €137.
h1_main: 7 Best Dinner Cruises in Dubai in 2026
author_role: 7 Dubai dinner cruises compared on boat type, route, menu, drinks, show, price per hour and transfers
lead: For most people, the right Dubai dinner cruise is the €52 Marina glass boat with an open bar. You get 90 minutes past Ain Dubai, JBR and Dubai Harbour, an international buffet with live pasta and noodle stations, and unlimited beer, wine and spirits in the price. No other dinner cruise on this list includes alcohol in its base fare.

The common mistake is booking a €22 wooden dhow and expecting the same night. The budget dhows are rated almost a full point lower (3.8–3.9 out of 5) and leave alcohol out of the package, and the cheapest one gives dinner a 45-minute slot. They are fine for a cheap Tanoura show on the water, as long as you know that is what you are buying.

If you would rather see the Burj Khalifa than the Marina towers, pick the canal route: a glass-enclosed dhow under the Sheikh Zayed Road waterfall bridge for €51, or €137 with a Gold Pass for La Perle afterwards. Want a seated multi-course dinner instead of a buffet? That is the €104 Michelin-chef menu on a Marina yacht.
Below are 7 dinner cruises side by side on boat type, route, buffet vs set menu, drinks, show, duration, price per hour and transfer. Filter by dhow, mega-yacht, open bar, budget or show included.

review: This is the benchmark every other cruise on the page gets measured against. €52 buys 90 minutes, a full buffet and an open bar, which works out at about €35 per hour on the water. The canal cruise at #2 costs almost the same but charges extra for alcohol, and the Michelin-menu yacht at #3 sells drinks at the bar on top of €104. If you plan on two or three drinks, the open bar alone covers a large part of the fare.

The boat is a modern two-deck vessel: glass-enclosed below with panoramic views, open-air above. The route stays in the Marina and Dubai Harbour area, so the views are Ain Dubai, the JBR towers and the Marina skyline lit up at night, not Downtown. Food is a continental and oriental buffet with two live cooking stations, which is more than the standard tray buffet on the cheaper dhows.

The trade-off is the mood. Music is soft and romantic rather than a show, so families hoping for a Tanoura dancer should look at #5 or the dhows. And at 90 minutes, it is a dinner, not a full evening. Pair it with something earlier in the day, like a Burj Khalifa slot, and you have the classic Dubai day.

review: This is the cruise to book if your mental picture of a Dubai dinner cruise includes the Burj Khalifa. Instead of the Marina towers, the canal route runs from Dubai Festival City past Al Jaddaf, Dubai Creek Harbour, Business Bay and the JW Marriott Marquis, then under the Dubai Canal Waterfall Bridge on Sheikh Zayed Road. At €51 for 2–2.5 hours it costs about the same as #1 but gives you roughly an extra hour on the water, around €20–25 per hour.

The boat is the hybrid of this page: a dhow in shape, glass-encased so you dine indoors. Boarding starts with Arabic kahwah, dates and chilled refreshments, then a buffet of Arabic appetisers, grilled meat, salads and Arabian sweets with live stations, with Arabic music and a saxophone set.

Two catches. Alcohol is an optional paid add-on, so if you drink, the real price climbs above #1. And entertainment is not available during Ramadan. Hotel pickup and drop-off is an option at booking, which matters here because Festival City is a long way from Marina and JBR hotels. review: Every other cruise on this page is a buffet. This one is a seated, multi-course dinner from a menu created by a Michelin-starred chef, served at your table on a luxury yacht between 8:00 and 10:00 PM. That changes the evening: no queue at the trays, no juggling plates on a moving deck, and a pace closer to a restaurant than a party boat.

At €104 for 2 hours, about €52 per hour, it is the priciest per hour of the dinner-only cruises. Included are unlimited soft drinks, water, coffee and tea, a live singer, Wi-Fi and toilets. Alcohol is sold at the full licensed bar on board, so a couple drinking wine will pay well above the headline fare. Compared with #1, you trade the open bar for better food and a calmer room.

It sails from Dubai Harbour Yacht Club through the Marina, the same skyline as #1, and transfers cost extra. It is not suitable for people prone to seasickness or with back, heart or blood pressure problems. The rating base is still small, so treat 4.5 as promising rather than proven. If you are already staying on the Palm, see our Palm Jumeirah hotel picks: Dubai Harbour is a short taxi away.

review: La Perle is one of Dubai's big evening tickets, and this bundle saves you planning two things around dinner. You board a luxury dhow at 6:15 PM behind InterContinental Dubai Festival City, sail the Dubai Water Canal for about 1.5 hours with an international buffet, pass the Burj Khalifa and glide under the sensor-operated Sheikh Zayed Road waterfall bridge, then get dropped at La Perle for the show with a Gold Pass.

At €137 it is the most expensive line on the page, but it is really two products. The canal dinner alone (#2) is €51, so you are paying roughly €86 on top for the Gold seats, the drop-off at the theatre and, if you choose it, the return shared transfer for hotels within 20 km.

It is also the best-rated option here at 4.9, on a smaller base of reviews. Small print worth knowing: house beverages only come with the option that includes them (or are bought on board, 21+), confirmed al fresco seating is 50 AED extra, the dress code is smart casual and it is not suitable for children under 2.

review: This is the entertainment-heavy Marina cruise: a traditional Tanura dance, live music, a live DJ and a Darbuka drum show on a modern catamaran. For €41 (down from €58) you get a 2-hour sightseeing sail past Ain Dubai, Bluewaters Island, Dubai Harbour and JBR, an international buffet from the Copthorne Hotel kitchen with BBQ, hot mains and vegetarian dishes, and unlimited water, soft drinks, tea and coffee.

It suits families best because nothing on the boat depends on alcohol: none is listed, and selected packages add mocktails, milkshakes or ice cream instead. You choose the air-conditioned lower deck or the open-air upper deck when booking, it is wheelchair accessible, and the guide speaks Arabic, English, French, Hindi and Tagalog.

At about €20 per hour on the water, it costs about €15 an hour less than #1, but the open bar is the difference. Hotel pickup is an extra charge and has to be arranged at least 6 hours ahead. If your family wants another evening show with dinner, the desert safaris also end with a Tanoura dancer and BBQ.

review: This is the cheapest way to eat dinner on the water in Dubai: €22, down from €27, for a 1.5-hour dhow sail from Dream Sea Lounge at Dubai Harbour Yacht Club. Included are the cruise, a buffet of international and local dishes and live entertainment: music, a Tanoura dance and a puppet show. At about €14 per hour, nothing else here comes close on price.

The trade-offs are real, and the 3.9 rating reflects them. The itinerary gives dinner a 45-minute window, alcohol is not part of the package and no soft-drink package is listed, and there is no hotel transfer, so add your taxi to Dubai Harbour. The boat leaves from Dubai Harbour, so expect Marina and Harbour views, not the old Creek.

Book it if the goal is a cheap, cheerful dhow evening with a Tanoura show. If dinner quality or drinks matter, the extra €19 for #5 (unlimited soft drinks, a hotel-kitchen buffet, 2 hours) or €30 for #1 (open bar) is money well spent. It is not suitable for pregnant travellers or people over 70.

guide.h2: Which Dubai Dinner Cruise Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Want drinks included? Book #1, €52 with unlimited beer, wine and spirits. Nothing else here includes alcohol.
  • Want the Burj Khalifa in view? Book #2 on the canal (€51), or #4 (€137) if La Perle is on your list.
  • Special occasion, food first? Book #3, the only seated multi-course menu, 8:00–10:00 PM.
  • Kids or no-alcohol group? Book #5: Tanura, live music, DJ and Darbuka, soft drinks included, wheelchair accessible.
  • Want the old Creek on a wooden dhow? Book #6, about €30 with optional hotel pickup, and accept a 3.8 rating.
  • Tightest budget? Book #7 at €22, a Tanoura show and a quick buffet, no transfer and no drinks package.

Dhow vs mega-yacht in one line: the wooden dhows (#6, #7) are about atmosphere and price; the modern boats (#1, #3, #5) win on food and comfort, and all rate well above the wooden dhows; the glass-enclosed canal dhows (#2, #4) give you the dhow look behind glass and the Downtown skyline.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Routes, Transfers and Hidden Extras
guide.html:
Marina vs Creek vs Canal

Marina and Dubai Harbour (#1, #3, #5, #7) means Ain Dubai, Bluewaters, JBR and the Marina towers lit up, with departures close to Palm and JBR hotels. Dubai Creek (#6) is the old trading waterway and the most traditional setting. Dubai Water Canal (#2, #4) boards at Al Faris Floating Restaurant in Dubai Festival City and is the only route that passes the Burj Khalifa and Business Bay.

Getting there

Transfers decide the real cost. #2, #4 and #6 offer pickup as a booking option, #3 and #5 charge extra (book #5's pickup at least 6 hours ahead), and #1 and #7 include none. Festival City is far from Marina hotels, so take the pickup option on the canal cruises if you are staying at JBR or on the Palm.

What costs extra

  • Alcohol on every cruise except #1 (paid add-on on #2, bar on #3, house beverages by option on #4, not included on #6 and #7, not listed on #5).
  • Souvenir photos on #4 and #5.
  • Confirmed al fresco seating on #4: 50 AED per person.
  • Tips on #7.

Timing and what to bring

#1 is back at the dock around 10:00 PM, #3 sails 8:00–10:00 PM and #4 boards at 6:15 PM for a 7:00 PM departure. Bring a camera and a light layer for the open upper decks. Large bags, strollers and outside alcohol are not allowed on the Dubai Harbour dhow (#7), and #4 asks for smart casual clothing. During Ramadan, check the show: #2 pauses its entertainment.

Planning the rest of the trip? Compare desert safaris with BBQ dinner for another evening, Burj Khalifa tickets for sunset from the top, or helicopter tours to see the Marina from above.

faqs.q: Which Dubai dinner cruise includes alcohol?
faqs.a: Only the Marina open-bar cruise (#1) includes unlimited beer, wine and spirits in its €52 fare. The canal cruises charge extra or include house beverages only on a higher option, the Michelin-chef yacht has a paid bar, and the dhows do not include alcohol.

faqs.q: Is a dhow cruise on Dubai Creek or Dubai Marina better?
faqs.a: The Creek is the traditional, old-Dubai setting; the Marina has the modern skyline with Ain Dubai and JBR. Ratings are higher on the Marina's modern boats. If you want the Creek specifically, #6 is the Creek dhow, about €30 with optional hotel pickup.

faqs.q: How much does a dinner cruise in Dubai cost?
faqs.a: From €22 per person for a basic Marina dhow to €52 for a glass boat with an open bar, €104 for a seated Michelin-chef menu and €137 for a canal dinner plus a La Perle Gold Pass.

faqs.q: Which dinner cruise passes the Burj Khalifa?
faqs.a: The Dubai Water Canal cruises (#2 and #4). They sail from Dubai Festival City through Business Bay, pass the Burj Khalifa and go under the Sheikh Zayed Road waterfall bridge. Marina cruises do not see the Burj Khalifa up close.

faqs.q: Are Dubai dinner cruises buffet or set menu?
faqs.a: Almost all are buffets, several with live cooking stations. The exception is #3, a seated multi-course menu created by a Michelin-starred chef, 8:00–10:00 PM from Dubai Harbour.

faqs.q: Which dinner cruise is best for kids?
faqs.a: #5, the Marina catamaran: Tanura dance, live music, a DJ and a Darbuka show, unlimited soft drinks, a choice of air-conditioned or open deck and wheelchair access. Note that #4 is not suitable for children under 2.

faqs.q: Can I cancel a Dubai dinner cruise?
faqs.a: All 7 cruises here offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before, and you can reserve now and pay later.

methodology: We compared 7 of Dubai's most popular dinner cruises side by side, across wooden dhows, glass-enclosed canal dhows and modern yachts. Each one was scored on boat type, route (Marina, Creek or Canal), buffet vs set menu, what drinks are included, entertainment, time on the water, price per hour and transfer options, using live from-prices for a normal evening. A near-identical second dhow from the same Dubai Harbour berth was left out so every card is a different choice.
